name: SLM Corporation (Sallie Mae)

profile.description: SLM Corporation (Sallie Mae Bank) originates and services private education loans for students and families and funds them with retail deposits such as high-yield savings, money market accounts and CDs. It is headquartered in Newark, Delaware. In Q3 2026 it posted a GAAP net loss of $32M (-$0.19 per share) as provisions rose with record originations growth: private education loan originations rose 15% to $3.4B and graduate originations rose 119%. Management cut FY2026 EPS guidance to $1.95-2.05 from $3.10-3.20 [1][2][6].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Sallie Mae has opened a meaningful new growth channel in graduate lending. Graduate loan originations rose 119% YoY in Q3 2026, driving total private education originations up 15% to $3.4B, the fastest year-over-year origination growth in its history [1][6]. AI Deployment (0/2): The February 2026 hiring of Steve Turner as Chief Technology and Enablement Officer, a digital transformation executive from Walgreens, aims to strengthen the technology foundation and drive innovation. No AI products or quantified AI savings were found [8]. Market Share (1/2): Sallie Mae is a major private student lender with share momentum in graduate loans, but research found no quantified share data [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management is investing ahead of origination growth, but has given no named products with revenue timelines [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D spending is reported [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Helping students and families finance higher education is a clear purpose, but Sallie Mae's articulation is not distinctive among consumer lenders [10]. Community Impact (1/2): The Sallie Mae Fund awarded $690,000 in grants for social-justice causes, and the company publishes GRI-referenced ESG reports. This is genuine but modest giving for a company with $567M of TTM net income [3][10]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (1/2): Insider activity is neutral, with no open-market purchases and almost no sales in Q2-Q3 2026 (5,488 shares disposed). Even after the stock fell from about $31 to $17.80, no insider buying was recorded [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically (Dividend sleeve; 8 straight years paid and a 2.92% yield): D/E of 285.3% (0.06), ROE of 23.6% (1.00), YoY revenue change of -21.4% in Q3 2026 (0.00; the year-ago quarter included a loan-sale gain), 5-year revenue CAGR of 5.8% (0.72), forward P/E of 5.9 on FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.00 (1.00), TTM net margin of 19.6% (0.98), payout ratio of 18.6% (1.00), 8 consecutive years paid since the 2019 reinstatement (0.80, 2x), 0 consecutive years of growth because the 2026 dividend is flat at $0.52 (0.00), and 5-year dividend CAGR of 21.1% (1.00, 2x). Weighted sum is 8.36/12, which rounds to 7 [3][4][7]. Payout is derived from the $0.52 dividend and TTM EPS of $2.79; FMP's reported 122% TTM payout conflicts with its own TTM EPS. Daily dollar volume is about $50M.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Sallie Mae is a chartered, FDIC-insured bank that funds loans with deposits. Its core economics come from balance-sheet lending, regulatory capital and its school-channel relationships, which AI cannot replace [1][3]. AI-native fintech underwriters and AI-driven servicing could compress pricing and raise customer-acquisition competition, and the company's own Q3 credit issue (charge-offs tied to misaligned third-party debt-resolution practices) shows operational processes are being reshaped [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue is reported; the new CTO's mandate is foundational modernization [8].

infinite_game.summary: Sallie Mae has a real role in helping families pay for college, but in Sinek's terms its recent history leans finite. Share count fell from 315M in 2021 to 186M, funded partly by loan sales, and a sudden 36% guidance cut followed back-to-back misses. Management's willingness to absorb upfront provisions for record graduate-loan growth, along with orderly succession planning, keeps it from the bottom of the scale.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Financing higher education is service-oriented, but Sallie Mae's purpose reads as a product description rather than an idealistic future state. Research found no evidence that it drives strategic trade-offs, and capital return has dominated recent allocation [3][10].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable under CEO Jon Witter (since 2020). In April 2026 the CFO and COO were named co-presidents as part of formal succession planning [7][9]. No employee-sentiment data was found to show exceptional trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Research found no management commentary framing competitors in private student lending or refinancing as rivals that improve Sallie Mae's own offering. Messaging centers on origination growth and share capture [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has reshaped itself into a focused, deposit-funded private education bank, now operating under the SLM Corporation name adopted in 2013 [3]. It is leaning into graduate lending, with 119% origination growth in Q3 2026 [1]. These are adaptations within one business line rather than a cause-driven reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management chose to absorb $214M of Q3 2026 provisions and a 36% FY2026 EPS guidance cut rather than slow record origination growth, accepting near-term pain for a larger loan book [1][6]. Years of aggressive buybacks, with the share count down about 40% since 2021 and partly funded by loan sales, are the kind of financial engineering Sinek views skeptically [3].

investment_thesis: After falling from a 52-week high of $31.06 to $17.80, Sallie Mae trades at about 5.9x FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.00, roughly 1.46x book, and a 2.92% dividend yield covered about 5x by TTM earnings [3][4][7]. Q3 2026 showed accelerating demand rather than shrinking franchise value: private education originations rose 15% to $3.4B, graduate originations rose 119%, and much of the GAAP loss reflects upfront CECL provisions booked on new loans [1][6]. TTM ROE is still 23.6%, and consensus expects EPS to recover to $3.67 by FY2028 if credit normalizes [3][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is credibility and credit. FY2026 EPS guidance was cut 36% to $1.95-2.05 after a second consecutive miss, and net charge-offs of $90M were tied to misaligned third-party debt-resolution practices. That raises questions about collections oversight and potential regulatory scrutiny [2][6]. Leverage is high (D/E of 285%), revenue fell 21% YoY against a quarter that included a loan sale, and rapid expansion into graduate loans brings new underwriting risk at scale [1][3]. The dividend has been flat at $0.13 per quarter since December 2024 [7].
key_catalysts: Q4 2026 delivery against the reset $1.95-2.05 EPS guide, which would restore management credibility after two consecutive misses
Seasoning of the record 2026 origination cohort, with graduate loans up 119%, converting upfront provisions into net interest income in 2027-2028
Resumption of loan sales or buybacks at about 1.46x book once capital and credit stabilize
key_risks: Credit deterioration and charge-offs from third-party debt-resolution practices, with potential CFPB or regulatory scrutiny
Underwriting risk from rapid scaling in graduate lending, a newer segment growing 119% YoY
Leverage of 285% D/E and sensitivity of deposit funding costs to rate moves
